::: {#def-coupled-model .definition name="T.5 The true tail and the full response" date="2026-10-12" export="def-coupled-model"}
Use @def-analytic. For $(h,a,b)\in\mathcal D_*$ and $0<k\le h$, set $L=1+h$ and define on $(0,L)$
$$
f_k(y)=\begin{cases}1-dy,&0<y<1,\\
\max\{p(1-x/h),q(1-x/k)_+\},&y=1+x,\ 0<x<h.
\end{cases}
$$
Let $A_0=A=\Pi\rho_+^2/2$ and $E=3\Pi\rho_+/S_0$. Denote by $\mu_k(A_0)$ the first eigenvalue of the full Friedrichs--Dirichlet realization with nonnegative potential $V_k=A_0/f_k^2$. The functions have zero trace at both outer endpoints and a common value at the interface $y=1$. The side Dirichlet--Dirichlet problems impose an additional zero trace at that interface. If $E$ lies strictly below both side first eigenvalues, use the unique trace-one minimizing extensions $g_H,g_T$ in @lem-interface and define
$$
\mathfrak d_H(E)=g_H'(1),\qquad
\mathfrak d_T^{\rm coupled}(E)=-g_T'(1).
$$
:::

::: {.proof of="def-coupled-model"}
By @def-analytic, $p>0$, $q\ge0$, $0<w=p+q<1$, and $h>0$. The head width is at least $w>0$. The tail width is at least $p(1-x/h)>0$, with a positive lower bound on compact interior subintervals. If $k<h$, the second branch vanishes when $x$ is sufficiently close to $h$; if $k=h$, the width equals $m(1-x/h)$. Thus the potential is bounded on either side near the interface, and near the right endpoint it is a constant multiple of $(L-y)^{-2}$. The one-dimensional right-end Hardy inequality $\int u^2/(L-y)^2\le4\int|u'|^2$ holds on $H_0^1(0,L)$: prove it on the smooth core by integration by parts and Cauchy--Schwarz, then extend by density. Consequently the potential form norm is equivalent to the $H_0^1$ norm, the form is closed, and the core is dense. The representation theorem for closed nonnegative forms gives a unique Friedrichs operator. Compact embedding and the interval Poincare inequality give a positive first eigenvalue that is attained. The interface-zero side forms have the same properties. Responses are defined only below the prescribed side Dirichlet eigenvalues; existence, uniqueness, and derivative traces of their minimizing extensions follow from @lem-interface.
:::

::: {#lem-coupled-response-lower-bound .lemma name="R.6.3 and T.5.2 A lower bound for the true common-interface response" date="2026-10-12" export="lem-coupled-response-lower-bound"}
For all parameters in @def-coupled-model, both side first Dirichlet eigenvalues are strictly greater than $E$, and
$$
\mathfrak d_H(E)+\mathfrak d_T^{\rm coupled}(E)\ge\mathcal G(h,a,b).
$$
If $(h,a,b)\in\mathcal D$, the right-hand side is strictly positive and $\mu_k(A_0)>E$.
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-coupled-response-lower-bound"}
Use @def-coupled-model and @def-analytic. By @lem-pole-free, the first Dirichlet eigenvalues of the head and model tail exceed $E$, $0<A_0<1$, $0<K=E-A_0<\Pi$, $1<\sigma<5/2$, $T=h^2E$ lies below the scaled model-tail first eigenvalue, and $r,C,D>0$. The model-tail potential is $V_m(1+x)=A_0/[m^2(1-x/h)^2]$.

Since $k\le h$, we have $0\le(1-x/k)_+\le1-x/h$ for $0<x<h$. Hence $f_k(1+x)\le m(1-x/h)$, and the true tail potential is at least the model potential. Both zero-trace form domains are $H_0^1(1,L)$, by the right-end Hardy inequality and local boundedness of the potentials. Rayleigh comparison makes the true tail first Dirichlet eigenvalue at least the model value, and therefore strictly greater than $E$. The head bound also follows from @lem-pole-free, so the two spectral hypotheses of @lem-interface hold.

To identify the head ODE solution with the variational minimizer, note that its potential is bounded and smooth on $[0,1]$. The solution belongs to $H^2(0,1)$, with endpoint traces zero and one. Integration by parts against smooth zero-trace tests gives orthogonality for the shifted form, which extends by $H_0^1$ density to the full side zero-trace domain. Since $E$ lies below the first side Dirichlet eigenvalue, the shifted form is coercive on the zero-trace subspace. Any other function with the same traces differs from the solution by a zero-trace function $z$, and its energy difference is $Q_E(z)>0$ unless $z=0$. Thus the solution is exactly the unique trace-one minimizing extension of @lem-interface.

The head potential is $A_0/(1-dy)^2$, and its normalized minimizing extension is the solution of @lem-head-response. The bounds $0<A_0<1<2$ and $0<K<\Pi$ check all parameter hypotheses. That lemma and @lem-cot-rational give
$$
\mathfrak d_H(E)\ge\mathsf H(K)+\mathcal B(A_0,w).
$$

For the model tail, set $z=(h-x)/h$. Its equation becomes $-u''+\sigma(\sigma-1)z^{-2}u=Tu$, because $A_0h^2/m^2=\Pi R^2/2=\sigma(\sigma-1)$. By @lem-tail-recurrence, its regular solution gives model response $D_\sigma(T)/h\ge\mathsf T(\sigma,T)/h$. The factor $1/h$ comes from $-\partial_x u((h-x)/h)=u'(z)/h$ at the interface $z=1$, followed by division by $u(1)>0$ for trace-one normalization.

The hypotheses of @lem-regular-tail hold with $s=\sigma>1$ and $T=h^2E$ below the scaled first Dirichlet eigenvalue. That lemma gives positivity, finite endpoint form energy, and the regular asymptotics
$$
u_s=z^s(1+O(z^2)),\qquad
u_s'=s z^{s-1}+O(z^{s+1}).
$$
It also identifies $u_s/u_s(1)$ as the unique trace-one minimizing extension on $(0,1)$. Under $z=(h-x)/h$, the physical shifted form is $1/h$ times the normalized shifted form at energy $T=h^2E$. Hence
$$
g_m(1+x)=\frac{u_s((h-x)/h)}{u_s(1)}
$$
is exactly the model-tail minimizing extension of @lem-interface, with interface trace one, zero outer trace, and outward response $D_s(T)/h$. The normalization and both response comparisons use the same physical interface and energy.

The common affine trace-one form domain must also be checked. Since $p>0$ and $f_k(y)\ge p(L-y)/h$ for $1<y<L$, we have $0\le V_k(y)\le A_0h^2/[p^2(L-y)^2]$. The model potential $A_0h^2/[m^2(L-y)^2]$ satisfies the same bound. For $z\in H_0^1(1,L)$, right-end Hardy gives $\int z^2/(L-y)^2\le4\int|z'|^2$. Both zero-trace form domains are therefore exactly $H_0^1(1,L)$, rather than merely being related by inclusion.

Choose one common smooth lifting $\psi$ with value one at $y=1$, supported in a right-hand neighborhood of the interface where the potentials are bounded, and vanishing near $L$. It has finite energy for both potentials. Any $u\in H^1(1,L)$ with $u(1)=1,u(L)=0$ satisfies $u-\psi\in H_0^1(1,L)$; Hardy's bound and the finite energy of the lifting make both weighted integrals finite. Conversely, elements of either trace-one form domain have these Sobolev traces. Thus the affine domains are both $\psi+H_0^1(1,L)$. The pointwise potential comparison and minimization below take place on this same set.

For a fixed interface trace, the minimum shifted energy is nondecreasing under pointwise increase of the nonnegative potential: compare the energies function by function on the common affine domain and take infima. By @lem-interface, each minimum is the corresponding outward response. Thus the true coupled-tail response is no smaller than the model response. Adding the head inequality gives the claimed full response bound.

For completeness, compactness for the full interval follows explicitly as well. The true full potential is bounded on the head and near the interface, and the tail satisfies $V_k\le A_0h^2/[p^2(L-y)^2]$. Endpoint Hardy therefore makes the full form domain $H_0^1(0,L)$, with equivalent form and $H_0^1$ norms, closed form, and dense smooth core. The complete model potential has the same properties. Nonnegativity makes either form norm control the full $H^1$ norm; Rellich's compact embedding $H_0^1(0,L)\hookrightarrow L^2(0,L)$ gives compactness for both full form domains. The interface-zero side forms are compactly embedded for the same reason. Thus every compactness hypothesis of the strict interface criterion is satisfied.

The true potential is bounded on both sides near the interface, and its form is closed and compactly embedded, so @lem-interface applies. If the point belongs to $\mathcal D$, then @lem-terminal gives $\mathcal G>0$. The common-interface response is strictly positive, and the strict spectral criterion in @lem-interface gives $\mu_k(A_0)>E$.
:::

::: {#lem-middle-spectral-closure .lemma name="T.5.2--T.5.3 Closure of the middle-height spectral contradiction" date="2026-10-12" export="lem-middle-spectral-closure"}
There are no data satisfying @def-candidate with $3/8<h\le4$. More explicitly, if such data existed, setting $a=\beta/h,b=Lq/h$ would give a point in $\mathcal D$ of @def-analytic, and $\rho_+=\beta/[h(h+2)]$, $A_0=\Pi\rho_+^2/2$, and $\overline E=3\Pi\rho_+/S_0$ would satisfy the contradictory spectral bounds
$$
\mu(A_0)>\overline E,\qquad
\mu(A_0)\le\frac2S\left(\Pi\rho+\frac{A_0}{\rho}\right)
<\frac{3\Pi\rho_+}{S}\le\overline E.
$$
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-middle-spectral-closure"}
Use @def-candidate and @def-analytic. The first assertion of @lem-robin places the parameter image in $\mathcal D$. The original candidate has $0<k\le h$, and its piecewise maximum width is exactly $f_k$ from @def-coupled-model. Hence the first eigenvalue of the corresponding full Friedrichs--Dirichlet operator equals $\mu_k(A_0)$. By @lem-coupled-response-lower-bound, $\mu(A_0)>\overline E$.

On the other hand, the candidate's longitudinal spectral bound gives $\rho\ge S/(2L^2)$. Its inequalities $\beta\le h$, $S=1+\beta+\gamma>1+\beta$, and $\gamma>0$ imply
$$
\frac\rho{\rho_+}\ge\frac{Sh(h+2)}{2\beta L^2}
\ge\frac{(1+\beta)h(h+2)}{2\beta L^2}
\ge\frac{h+2}{2L}>\frac12.
$$
The outer-ear bound gives $\rho<\rho_+$. For $x=\rho/\rho_+\in(1/2,1)$,
$$
\frac32-x-\frac1{2x}=\frac{(1-x)(2x-1)}{2x}>0.
$$
The all-weight necessary condition in @def-candidate, applied to this same $A_0>0$, gives $\mu(A_0)\le2(\Pi\rho+A_0/\rho)/S<3\Pi\rho_+/S$. Also $q=\gamma/(1+k)$ and $\gamma\le k$ imply $q/(1-q)=\gamma/(1+k-\gamma)\le\gamma$, so $S_0=\beta+1/(1-q)\le\beta+1+\gamma=S$. The strict upper bound is therefore at most $3\Pi\rho_+/S_0=\overline E$, contradicting the strict lower bound already obtained.
:::
